summary: This program adds two numeric stream calculations to the farmers' market app: one that adds up the price of every product, and one that averages the price of only the organic products. Both work by turning the stream of products into a stream of plain double numbers with mapToDouble, which unlocks math operations like sum() and average().

lines.text: This stands in for the list of MarketProduct objects built in the earlier exercises; the book omits it here so the new stream code stays in focus.
Calls the helper below and stores the single number it returns, keeping the calculation separate from the printing.
String.format with "%.2f" rounds the double to two decimal places, so a money value prints as 24.50 rather than 24.499999999999996.
The method returns a double because the answer is a single total, not a list; each stream question gets its own small, testable method.
Converts the stream of products into a DoubleStream of prices, which is the stream type that offers arithmetic methods.
Adds every price in the DoubleStream and returns the total; an empty list simply yields 0.0.
Keeps only the products whose isOrganic method returns true, so the average that follows is computed on organic items alone.
Returns an OptionalDouble rather than a double, because a stream with no elements has no average to report.
Unwraps the OptionalDouble, supplying 0.0 when no organic products were found so the caller never has to handle an empty result.
